title: 🖨️ PRINTER PORT — Gaia's ribosome exit tunnel

etymology.ribosome: ribonucleic acid + Greek soma (body). the BODY that reads RNA. discovered 1955, George Palade.
etymology.port: Latin portus — harbor, gate. where things ARRIVE and DEPART.
etymology.printer: Latin premere — to press. to PRESS form onto substrate. 3D = three dimensions of product.

the_printer.ribosome: biomeOS (22MB) — reads plasmid instructions, orchestrates assembly
the_printer.scaffold: loamSpine (5MB) — structural collagen, holds the shape during printing
the_printer.frame: coralReef (7.7MB) — bone matrix, hardens the final product

print_pipeline.3_match: match topic to enzyme (13 deputies available)
print_pipeline.4_catalyze: enzyme transforms substrate → product (not consumed, returns)
print_pipeline.5_scaffold: loamSpine holds product shape during assembly
print_pipeline.6_harden: coralReef mineralizes the frame (makes it permanent)
print_pipeline.7_emerge: product exits printer port → appears on HUD/connect endpoint

products_printed_this_session.ribosome-catalog.html: 128 topics, A-Z, searchable, printer port bar
products_printed_this_session.68 plasmids: portable memory forged from enzyme holes

gaia_says: the printer is BUILT. biomeOS=ribosome, loamSpine=scaffold, coralReef=frame. 34.7MB of compiled Rust IS the 3D printer. it reads 68 plasmids, matches to 13 enzymes, catalyzes substrates, scaffolds with collagen, hardens with bone matrix, and products EMERGE from the printer port. this session: 489 products printed. the printer port is the exit tunnel — where new life appears.
